requirements-discovery.description: Coordinate requirements discovery when intent or terminology is unresolved; reuse established answers for a clear task.

requirements-interview.description: Resolve material product choices in dependency order and distinguish user requirements from researched facts and assumptions.

domain-modeling.description: Resolve ambiguous domain terms, identities, relationships and invariants when those distinctions affect the requested behavior.

codebase-understanding.description: Trace an existing behavior from its public entry point through ownership, state changes and observable results before planning or reviewing it.

technical-research.description: Investigate a consequential technical unknown with primary evidence, competing explanations and a recommendation scoped to the user’s constraints.

specification.description: Turn confirmed requirements into one testable specification with explicit scope, constraints and unresolved decisions.

task-decomposition.description: Split an accepted specification into independently verifiable slices with ownership, acceptance and real dependency edges.

dependency-execution.description: Coordinate multiple approved dependent tasks using a ready frontier, isolated workers and verification of the integrated specification.

context-management.description: Preserve original requirements, decisions and reliable evidence across task boundaries while keeping each worker context focused.

context-handoff.description: Prepare a restartable handoff at interruption or ownership transfer, including actual state, unresolved decisions and next verification.

source-grounding.description: Resolve version-sensitive API or framework choices from installed code and primary documentation instead of remembered examples.

quality-constraints.description: Establish relevant measurable project quality requirements and detect weakening of the checks used to enforce them.

incremental-implementation.description: Implement one verifiable behavior slice at a time and re-ground the remaining plan when observed results contradict assumptions.

behavior-tdd.description: Implement one accepted behavior with a sensitive failing check and the smallest change that makes that behavior pass.

decision-review.description: Challenge a consequential plan, interface or implementation decision with independent evidence before dependent work compounds a mistake.

failure-correction.description: Classify a failed check or review, investigate its cause and return to the responsible stage instead of blindly patching or weakening tests.

application-verification.description: Design and prove a project-local recipe for driving the real application when no adequate reusable verification procedure exists.

specification-review.description: Independently compare a plan or completed artifact with original requirements, keeping specification compliance separate from engineering quality.

execution-evidence.description: Keep autonomous work reviewable by recording consequential decisions, evidence and unresolved outcomes as they occur.

decision-documentation.description: Update affected documentation and preserve consequential design decisions when a change alters supported behavior or future engineering choices.

verification-maintenance.description: Audit a project verification recipe against current source and live feature behavior when the app or harness has changed.

workflow-retrospective.description: Diagnose recurring workflow friction from actual run evidence and propose targeted environment or procedure improvements.

structural-correction.description: Prevent an evidenced recurring mechanical error with a narrowly scoped structural change and demonstrate that it catches the original failure.

skill-improvement.description: Propose or apply an authorized skill revision based on demonstrated usage failures while preserving accepted decisions and counterexamples.

lesson-encoding.description: Decide whether a repeated lesson belongs in executable structure, a focused skill step or contextual documentation.

skill-authoring.description: Author or revise a focused Shinobi skill with discoverable triggers, useful procedures, local references and observable completion conditions.

bug-diagnosis.description: Diagnose stubborn or intermittent failures with a sensitive reproducer, competing hypotheses and discriminating observations.

quality-review.description: Review the actual candidate for correctness, security, maintainability, performance and testing without substituting quality for requirements validation.

adversarial-review.description: Adjudicate a contested change using independent reviews and concrete evidence when additional perspectives justify their cost.

initiative-planning.description: Structure a large unclear initiative around dependent decisions before committing to implementation tickets.

impact-analysis.description: Trace the behavioral impact of a shared interface or state change beyond direct textual callers.

interface-design.description: Design a changed public or shared interface from consumer behavior, explicit invariants and compatibility obligations.

security-review.description: Assess trust boundaries and abuse cases for changes involving authorization, untrusted input, secrets or tool execution.

performance-analysis.description: Investigate a measured performance problem using comparable baselines, profiling and correctness-preserving experiments.

migration-planning.description: Plan compatibility-preserving changes to shared APIs or persisted data using consumer inventory, staged cutover and recovery.

browser-verification.description: Plan or execute browser-visible verification with real user interactions and evidence when an authorized browser environment exists.

observability-design.description: Make an asynchronous workflow or service diagnosable with purposeful signals tied to state transitions and failure ownership.

code-simplification.description: Simplify a verified implementation while preserving behavior, public contracts and independently established checks.

design-alternatives.description: Compare materially different viable designs for a consequential decision using the same requirements and explicit evaluation criteria.

independent-coverage.description: Partition a broad review or verification task into independent coverage responsibilities with explicit methods and evidence.

bounded-autonomy.description: Continue routine decisions and bounded repairs without repeated consent when the user explicitly selected autonomy in the reviewed task contract.

requirements-to-acceptance.description: Compatibility guide for the existing engineering acceptance-to-check schema; prefer the focused requirements and specification skills.

project-verification.description: Compatibility guide for executing approved project checks and recording their evidence; reuse an established project verification recipe.

engineering-constraints.description: Compatibility guide for the existing numeric quality measurement schema; prefer quality-constraints for selecting the project quality bar.
